verses.1: In the year of Ben-Shmonah, Josiah ruled as king. He ruled for thirty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Yedida, from Betzkat.
verses.2: And he did what was right in the eyes of Jehovah. He followed all the ways of his father David. He never turned to the right or left.
verses.3: In those years, King Josiah reigned. The king sent Shaphan, son of Azariah, son of Meshulam, the scribe in the house of God, to do this work.
verses.4: Let the high priest go up to Hilkia, and let them take away the money that has been collected in the house of Jehovah from among the people.
verses.5: And it shall be given to those who work in the house of Jehovah. They will give it to those who work in the house of Jehovah, so that they may strengthen the door of the house.
verses.6: For those who are young and those who are old, as well as for those who are building houses, and for those who are buying wood and stone to strengthen their homes.
verses.7: But do not consider the money given to them as something that they have earned in their own efforts. In truth, they are simply doing what they are supposed to do.
verses.8: And the high priest Hilkiah said to the scribe, “I have found the Book of the Law in the house of the LORD.” Then Hilkiah handed the book to the scribe and called out his name.
verses.9: And the scribe came before the king. He asked the king to take away the money that had been found in the house. The king gave it to the workers who were responsible for maintaining the temple.
verses.10: And Shaphan, the scribe, reported to the king, “The priest gave me a portion of it.” Then Shaphan called out its name before the king.
verses.11: And when the king heard the words of the Book of the Torah, he tore his clothes in anger.
verses.12: And the king commanded that Hilkiya, the priest, and Ahikam son of Shaphan, and Acbor son of Michaias, along with Shaphan the scribe, and Asiya, the servant of the king, should be appointed to carry out these tasks.
verses.13: Go, and seek out Jehovah for me, for the sake of the people and for the sake of all of Judah. Let them take this book seriously, because it is a great blessing from Jehovah. It was given to us so that we might follow all the laws written in it. Our ancestors did not listen to these words in the past; now they must obey them.
verses.14: And Hilkiah, the priest, and Ahikam, and Achbor, and Shaphan, and Asya, went to the prophetess Sheba who was the daughter of Ecionah, daughter of Echemas. She was the one who kept the sacred objects. She lived in Jerusalem during that time. They spoke to her.
verses.15: And He said to them, “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: ‘Say to the man who sent you to me, “’”
verses.16: So said Jehovah: “I will bring calamity upon this place and its rulers, in accordance with all the words written by King Yehuda.”
verses.17: Under the circumstances in which they abandoned me and set others as their gods, so that they could provoke me with all their actions. My zeal was extinguished in this place, but it will not be extinguished.
verses.18: And to the king of Judah, who has sent you to seek out Jehovah, say to him these words: “Thus says Jehovah, the God of Israel: These are the words that you have heard.”
verses.19: Because of your kindness of heart, you obeyed God’s commands. You listened to what I said about this place and its inhabitants, who were destined to be a source of shame and disgrace. You tore your clothes in anger and wept before me. And I too heard these words from God.
verses.20: Therefore, I will gather you with your ancestors. You will be brought back to your graves in peace. Your eyes will not see all the evil that I will bring upon this place. And the king will be restored to his rightful place.
